newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government long bonds closed lower on Thursday but off the day's low, while the shorter end of the yield curve ended little higher.

"The tone of the market is still positive, but people are scared of long positions on the long bonds," a dealer in Madrid said. "What we saw today was a flattening in the curve, because they bought two and three-year bonds".

Dealers added that the market will continue to be positive in the coming days "at least until we don't see any other remarks against EMU. In that case Spanish and Italian bonds could see a profit taking wave," a dealer said.
Bank of Spain's central governor Luis Angel Rojo said earlier that the economic situation is fairly favourable and he added that the country can reasonably aspire to form part of monetary union.
The market did not react to his words, dealers said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was little changed at 164 basis points, while the differential over Btp widened to 32 from 28 this morning at the start.
The peseta ended little weaker at 84.20/22 per mark versus 84.13/4.16 at the close yesterday.
